body.x: Uniqconn Inc. (CEO Young Dong Kim) participated in the “Global Media Meetup” hosted by AVING News’ International Press Club (IPC) for domestic companies and startups on Tuesday, December 9, at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul.

The Global Media Meetup focused on introducing Korean companies’ and startups’ products and technologies to the global market. In particular, it aimed to proactively share information on CES 2026 Innovation Award winners and CES-participating startups through global media channels and expand business opportunities.

Uniqconn was founded in 2022 by experts from multiple fields to address bottlenecks that occur in cable- and connector-based high-speed data transmission amid rapidly increasing data transfer speeds, while also improving user convenience.

The company is a fabless firm that designs and develops a single-chip solution capable of wirelessly transmitting data at 6.25 Gbps in the unlicensed 60 GHz band, and it also has in-house capabilities to design mmWave antennas using proprietary technology. Based on this foundation, Uniqconn specializes in providing technologies that replace existing wired interfaces with short-range, high-speed wireless connections for consumer electronics and industrial applications.

Leveraging this technological strength, Uniqconn collaborated with Samsung Electronics to verify and develop wireless solutions for debugging connectors exposed on the exteriors of home appliances, such as refrigerators and washing machines. This demonstrated its capability to process data wirelessly without cables during appliance assembly lines and after-sales service operations. In addition, by verifying wireless Ethernet data communication together with Germany’s Rosenberger, Uniqconn showed that its wireless data transmission technology has gained recognition overseas as well.

Through these efforts, Uniqconn has actively conducted technology validation projects and promotional activities with major domestic and global corporations, thereby presenting a new communication paradigm.

Against this backdrop, ahead of the opening of CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and technology exhibition to be held in Las Vegas, the United States, in January 2026, Uniqconn achieved the milestone of winning an Innovation Award for its small wireless chip ‘UC60,’ which enables high-speed wireless data transmission.

UC60 integrates a transmitter and a receiver into a single chip, enabling full-duplex communication with simultaneous two-way data transmission. The company explained that a key technical challenge was preventing interference from the transmitted signal from affecting the receiver.

To address this, the chip incorporates a dedicated isolation circuit that maintains signal clarity even when transmission and reception operate simultaneously. In addition, Uniqconn’s proprietary antenna technology provides additional external isolation, ensuring stable performance in real-world usage environments. The chip uses ASK modulation for data encoding.

Operating at 60 GHz, UC60 maintains ultra-low latency and high-reliability signal quality even at gigabit-class transmission speeds, making it well-suited for real-time streaming and interactive applications. This RF-based approach eliminates issues such as connector wear, corrosion, and electromagnetic interference (EMI), positioning the solution as a replacement for conventional connectors in applications requiring high-reliability, high-speed wireless data transmission, including docking stations, wearables, and fully sealed electronic devices.

The ultra-compact 3.5×3.5mm form factor of UC60 also has the potential to bring fundamental changes to electronic product design philosophy. By using flip-chip BGA packaging, the chip delivers high performance while occupying minimal PCB space, enabling smaller, slimmer product designs. By removing physical connectors, UC60 allows for smooth, portless exteriors, offering particular advantages for products where clean design matters, such as wearables, waterproof electronics, and premium consumer devices.

Furthermore, the wireless-based architecture removes existing constraints such as impedance matching issues and EMI associated with metal connectors. As a result, designers gain unprecedented freedom in component placement and routing, while also resolving reliability issues caused by connector wear and exposure to external environments.

body.x: UC60 also supports ultra-low-latency applications such as AR/VR, real-time gaming, and professional streaming, enabling next-generation user experiences that were previously difficult to realize.

The solution has also been recognized for its innovation as a wireless platform that supports high-speed wired protocols. A Uniqconn official said, “Existing wireless technologies such as Wi-Fi struggle to reliably handle high-speed wired protocols that require strict bit error rates and precise timing. Gigabit Ethernet, USB 3.0, and MIPI interfaces demand data integrity and reliability beyond what conventional wireless technologies can provide.” The official added, “UC60 is a wireless solution that can bridge this technical gap and meet the demanding performance standards required by high-speed wired protocols.”

The official continued, “UC60 has a unique capability to convert high-speed wired interfaces into wireless connections within conditions of one-to-one communication within two meters and power consumption below 1 watt. This technological innovation fundamentally resolves the trade-off that had been unavoidable between ‘wireless convenience’ and ‘high-performance data transmission.’”

In addition, UC60 features a ‘Tap-to-Connect’ approach, where a high-speed data link forms instantly when devices are brought close together. Because it does not require separate pairing or authentication procedures, it delivers an intuitive and immediate user experience that is difficult to achieve with conventional wireless technologies.

This technology enables a modular device ecosystem. For example, detachable smartphone cameras, stacked computing modules, and AR accessories can connect naturally through simple contact. Users can physically attach compatible components to expand device functionality and configure devices in the form they desire.

body.cap: Uniqconn CEO Young Dong Kim conducts interviews with media representatives from four countries, including the United States, France, the United Arab Emirates, and Taiwan. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: This connector-free design removes inconveniences associated with traditional structures, such as port wear, waterproofing issues related to moisture intrusion, and cable management, while maintaining professional-grade data transmission speeds. In this way, UC60 provides a foundation for next-generation modular electronic devices, in which hardware modularity matches the flexibility of software.

Uniqconn positions itself as a wireless communication technology company proposing a new communication paradigm and aims to spread its technology across global industrial markets. To achieve this, the company has set out to collaborate with international leading companies that exert a strong technological influence in each country as a core strategy.

Uniqconn stated, “Wireless data communication technology is not limited to a specific country or industry, and it can be applied wherever industrial sites exist. Accordingly, Uniqconn pursues a strategy of expanding communication infrastructure across the entire global market rather than focusing on specific regions.” The company added, “Our ultimate goal is to enable anyone around the world to experience Uniqconn’s unique wireless communication technology regardless of location. Through this, we aim to establish a new global standard for communication technology.”

Meanwhile, AVING News has introduced Korean companies to the world through partnership cooperation with more than 800 media outlets across 54 countries over the past 22 years. Building on its long-established global media network, AVING News launched the International Press Club in August. Media outlets participating in this Global Media Meetup included Innovation & Tech Today from the United States, Le Café Du Geek from France, Arageek from the United Arab Emirates, and Digitimes from Taiwan.
